title: UAP Disclosure Act eminent domain over privately held material

tellings.quote: this is why the UP disclosure act explicitly targeted eminent domain right for things held in private hands

(a) Exercise of Eminent Domain.--The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good.

plain: The claim is that a proposed US law ordered the government to take over any alien technology or remains held by private companies. The law is the UAP Disclosure Act. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's newer term for UFOs. Senators Chuck Schumer and Mike Rounds put it forward in the Senate on 13 July 2023 as an amendment to the NDAA, the yearly bill that funds the military. A researcher named Matthew Pines tells Michels that this is why the act "explicitly targeted eminent domain" over things held in private hands. Eminent domain is the government's power to take private property for public use. If he is right, Congress was acting on a belief that private firms hold such material. The other teller is the amendment's own text, and it is unusually direct. It says the federal government "shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good." On its face, the text matches Pines's account of what the act sets out to do.
